title: Premier Lig Seyir Defteri: Tottenham Hotspur ve Luca Williams-Barnett’ın yükselişi
summary: Bilir misiniz, İngiltere’de BBC’de yayınlanan enfes futbol programı "Match of the Day" (Günün Maçı) ilk kez 1964-65 sezonunun başında ekranlara geldi. O gün oynanan bir maçın önemli anları, o dönemde yalnızca Londra'da izlenebilen ‘BBC Two’ kanalında yayınlanacaktı. Ancak bu durum tartışmalara yol açtı, maç ekranlarda olunca taraftarlar maçlara gelmeye devam edecek miydi? Alt liglerde tribünlerin doluluk oranına etkisi ne olacaktı? O dönem Burnley’nin başkanlığın yapan Bob Lord, mabetleri Turf Moor'a kameraların girmesine izin vermeyi reddeden ilk kulüp başkanı oldu. Uzun tartışmalardan sonra uzlaşmaya varıldı, BBC televizyonda yayınlanacak Cumartesi maçının görüntülerini, tüm karşılaşmalar sona erene kadar ekrana getirmemeyi kabul etti. Kısa süre sonra canlı maç yayınlarına yönelik yasak (blackout) uygulaması geldi. 1987’de Avrupa'daki ulusal liglerde seyirci sayılarının düşmesi üzerine UEFA İngiltere'nin ortaya attığı fikri benimsedi ve tüzüğüne 48. maddeyi ekledi. Buna göre her ülke, en üst iki ligdeki maçların en az %50'sinin oynandığı zaman dilimlerinde, iki buçuk saatlik bir "yayınsız dönem" belirleyecekti. Bu uygulama, izleyicilerin farklı seviyelerdeki yerel futbol maçlarına gitmesini teşvik etmek, maç günleri tribünlerin dolmasını sağlamak amacıyla tasarlanmıştı. Günümüzde 48. madde'yi uygulayan yalnızca İngiltere, İskoçya ve Kuzey İrlanda ligleri. Başka hiçbir büyük ülkede "yayın yasağı" (blackout) uygulaması bulunmamakta çünkü başka hiçbir büyük ülkede, en üst ligden alt liglere kadar tüm kademeleri kapsayan ortak başlama saati uygulanmıyor. Maçların Cumartesi 15.00’de başlaması Ada futboluna özgü bir gelenek, haliyle naklen yayın meselesi farklı. Alman futbol meraklıları bilir, Bundesliga'nın kendine has başlama saati vardır, maçlar cumartesi saat 15:30’da başlar ve başka hiçbir lig kademesi bu saatte maç yapmaz. Örneğin Bundesliga 2’de maçlar genellikle Cumartesi günleri saat 13:30'da başlar. Diğer büyük liglerde de durum benzer. Özetle, başka ülkelerde yayın yasağı uygulaması bulunmuyor; çünkü futbol takvimi buralarda tamamen farklı bir işleyişe sahip. Geçenlerde BBC’de yayınlanan makalede, Premier Lig, EFL ve İskoçya Premiership'e ilişkin anlaşmaların 2029-30 sezonunda yenilenme aşamasına geleceği, bu durumun tüm önemli paydaşların bir araya gelerek yayın yasağına son verme konusunda anlaşmaya varmaları için bir fırsat sunacağı yazılıyordu. Ada futbolunda 60 senelik Cumartesi yayın yasağı geleneği yakında sona erecek mi bekleyip göreceğiz. Dönelim futbola, sevilmeyen milli maç molasından sonra Premier Lig’e dönüş, Cumartesi 15.00’te başlayan maçta arka arkaya kazandığı son üç maçtan sonra Leeds deplasmanından puansız dönen Tottenham evinde Ipswich Town karşısında. Leeds karşısında gol atmayı başaramayan Tottenham bu sezon beş maçta gol sevinci yaşayamadı, 33 senelik Premier Lig tarihinde sadece üç sezonda gol yollarında daha etkisiz kaldılar. Tottenham'ın bu sezon ligdeki en golcü ismi, iki golle stoper Jan Paul van Hecke. Asıl santrforlar Omar Marmoush ve Dominic Solanke'nin ise Premier Lig'de birer golü bulunuyor. Ipswich Town, Tottenham deplasmanında çıktığı 27 lig ve kupa maçının sekizini kazandı (4 beraberlik, 15 mağlubiyet); 2024-25 sezonunda sadece dört galibiyet alıp küme düşen takım Tottenham deplasmanında kazanmıştı, mavi beyazlılar Kuzey Londra’da arka arkaya iki maç kazanma hedefinde. Ev sahibi Tottenham 4-2-3-1 dizilişinde; kalede Kinsky, savunmada Porro, Van Hecke, Senesi, Udogie, orta sahada Gallagher, Fernandes, ileri uçta Kudus, Maddison, Williams-Barnett, önlerinde gol umutları Solanke. Misafir Ipswich aynı dizilişte; kalede Walton, savunmada Furlong, Diop, O'Shea, Davis, orta sahada Lukic, Palacios, ileri uçta Ouattara, Enciso, Maeda, önlerinde 9 numaralı Flemming. İlk bölümde oyunu kısa paslarla geriden kuran rakibi karşısında 3. bölgede baskıda mavi formalı Ipswich, bu sezon beş deplasman maçında bir galibiyet alırken dört puan topladı. 4. dakikada soldan geliştirdikleri atakta Ouattara’nın uzak direkte vuruşunda Tottenham kalesinde Kinsky gole izin vermiyor. 10’da arka arkaya kullandığı iki kornerde rakip savunmayı geçemiyor ev sahibi, solda 18 yaşındaki Williams-Barnett çabukluğuyla göze batan oyuncuları. İlk 15 dakikada topa yüzde 74 oranında sahip Tottenham rakip kaleyi üç kez yoklarken 15. dakikada golü buluyor. Porro’nun sağdan ortaladığı pozisyonda topa son dokunan Williams-Barnett, genç forvetin zamanlaması, arzusu, golde sergilediği fiziksel gücü etkileyici, kariyerinde önemli bir an. Geriye düştükten sonra hücuma kalabalık çıkıyor Ipswich Town, ancak rakip ceza sahasına girmekte zorlanıyorlar. 29’da ikinci gole yaklaşıyor Tottenham, Kudus’un kullandığı duran topta direkler gole izin vermiyor. 30’dan sonra iki takım da 2. bölgede top kayıpları yapıyor, 39’da Tottenham atağında Maddison müsait pozisyonda isabetsiz vuruyor, devrenin kırılma anlarından. Akabinde sarı kartı görüyor Tottenham’ın oyun kurucusu. 42’de Ipswich atağında Enciso duran topta rakip savunmayı geçemiyor, mücadele olarak iyiler ama gol yollarında etkisizler. Tottenham’ın topa yüzde 64 oranında sahip olduğu, rakip kaleyi 10 kez yokladığı iki dakika uzatılan devre tek gollü üstünlüğüyle kapanıyor. 2. devrenin başında takımlar aynı kadrolarla sahada. Devreye bıraktığı yerden, baskılı başlıyor Tottenham, 50’de sağdan kullandıkları kornerde Gallagher’dan önce rakip savunma topa müdahale ediyor. 52’de fark ikiye çıkıyor, Williams-Barnett’in soldan ortasına yakın mesafeden topu ağlara gönderen Solanke, sezonda ikinci golü. 56’da Ipswich’de üç değişiklik, Palacios, Maeda ve Ouattara yerlerini Florentino, Clarke ve Fatawu’ya bırakıyor. 64’te Tottenham’da Gallagher, Williams-Barnett ve Solanke’nin yerlerine Bergvall, Savio ve Marmoush sahada. Ligde ilk 11’da başladığı ilk maçta bir gol, bir asist yapan Williams-Barnett oyundan çıkarken ayakta alkışlanıyor. Akabinde 3. gole yaklaşıyorlar, Gallagher’ın ortasında savunmada O’Shea’ye çarpan topu sağına uzanarak çıkartıyor Walton, 31 yaşındaki 1.96’lık kaleci takımın iyilerinden. 74’te Ipswich forvet hattında Flemming’in yerini Emerson alıyor. 75’ten sonra farkı azaltma adına atakların sıklaştırıyor Ipswich, 76’da sağdan ortalanan topta Clarke’ın vuruşu savunmadan dönüyor. 79’da rakibe arkadan müdahalesi sonucu sarı karı gören Tottenham’da Kudus, pozisyon kırmızıya yakın. Son bölümde farkı azaltma adına rakip kaleye yükleniyor Ipswich, ancak final paslarında etkisizler. Altı dakika uzatılan maçta başka gol olmayınca 2-0 kazanan Tottenham maç fazlasıyla Everton’un üstüne, 9. sıraya yükseliyor. Ipswich’e gelince, bu sezon 11 maçta kalesinde 22 gol gören takım hiçbir maçta kalesini gole kapatamadı. Ligde beş maçtır kazanmıyorlar, savunma zaaflarının gideremezlerse lige tutunmaları zor olacaktır sanırım. Maçın adamı: kulüp tarihinde ilk 11'de başlayan en genç altıncı Tottenham oyuncusu oldu Williams-Barnett. 10 yaşında katıldığı takımda ilk 11’e yükselmesi, ilk maçında parlayışı takdire şayan.

title: The climate agenda of those defending life II: We must organise our own alternative
summary: Özge Güneş and İlkay Öz The fact that those defending their living spaces expect nothing at all from the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) rests on their experience with companies and the political authorities in their own regions. As they discuss the summit's financing pledges, its sponsors and the carbon market, one question keeps coming up: is a solution possible without changing the order of capital and politics that is causing the destruction? In the second part of our roundtable interview, we ask participants from Muğla, Artvin, Aydın, Arhavi and the Northern Forests about the reasons for their distrust and what can be done to grow the struggle. Their proposals, ranging from local solidarity to food sovereignty and from sharing experience to organising, also open up a discussion on how to act beyond criticism. What do you expect from COP31? And as an alternative to it, what kind of solidarity, organisation and demands do the struggles defending living spaces need in order to build an alternative of their own? WE EXPECT NOTHING FROM COP31 Esra Işık, Akbelen The COP summit is a very long way from being a place where the voices of the people could ever be heard. It is really a summit where international companies carve things up among themselves, asking "How do we hand our lands out to one another, how do we seize them?" That is why it is simply impossible for the demands of peasants, of working people, of those in this country and across the world who are hit hardest by the climate crisis, to be heard there. By its very structure and spirit, the COP31 summit is really a piece of theatre staged by those chiefly responsible for the plunder and the destruction we are living through, as if the solution lay with them, as if they actually wanted to solve it. And the curtain on this theatre rises in the very places where we live. If a real struggle is to be waged, this destruction can only be stopped in our villages, in our living spaces, through our own efforts and our own struggle. That is what we believe. From where we stand, there is currently no way forward other than direct struggle on the ground. Legal action is something we use to buy time on certain issues and to give our direct struggle something to stand on. That is why, today, without direct struggle, without the unity and solidarity of the people living in that region in particular, the peasants and the workers who live there and also work in the mines, without waging a genuine, real struggle, gains are very hard to come by. Unless real solidarity is built, winning is hard. If genuine, sincere solidarity is to be built today, genuine and sincere relationships must first be built with those regions. Whoever is going to show solidarity, whether groups, organisations, individuals or circles, must become one with the people of that region, the people of those villages. They must truly see the problems. In this process, they need to live through it alongside these people as well. You cannot stand up for these struggles by following them on the news now and then and having a rough idea of what is going on. That is why we need real organising, real coming together. These are not struggles that can be carried out solely by people coming from outside. They are struggles in which the people of the region must stand up for their own land and their own labour. Those who come in solidarity must also build genuine, sincere relationships within these struggles and breathe in and out with them. We believe we can change things through a process of solidarity that asks: "What is going on, what are the company's manipulations, and how do we break them?" One of our greatest gains in Akbelen is that the struggle has not stayed confined to our own region. Today, on the Perşembe Plateau, there are peasants and people in struggle whom we regard as our fellow travellers, our comrades. The same goes for Varto and for Artvin. A web of solidarity has been woven that reaches every corner of the country. This is one of our greatest gains. What needs to be done for it to grow? We need real solidarity that we think hard about, reflect on and put our labour into. IT IS NOTHING BUT THEATRE Tolga Odabaş, Green Artvin Association (Yeşil Artvin Derneği) The fact that Cengiz Holding is a sponsor already says it all. When you look at the graph for the last 30 years, covering every summit up to COP31, you see that not one of the commitments made has been met and that the curve keeps climbing. As Esra said, it is nothing but theatre. We are living in an order in which those who protect the environment are the ones who suffer most. By turning farmland into a car park, they have already made clear what they think COP31 is about. We do not have much hope. Once again, fake figures will be bandied about and loans tossed around. They will say, "We will provide financial support to developing countries." Yet we know full well whom and which investments they finance. We do not expect much from a setting in which there is a carbon market and carbon credits are bought and sold. A polluter can even offset the carbon it will emit by buying up the carbon stored in forests in other regions. This is also one of the greatest injustices of the climate crisis. The price of the damage done by the economic activities and capital groups most responsible for causing this crisis is very often paid by the people who benefit least from those activities. Those facing drought, floods, forest fires, the loss of their livelihoods and the destruction of their living spaces are mostly working people, peasants and local communities. Even so, these people have only a limited say in shaping climate policy. What we call climate justice is not just about reducing the amount of carbon. It is also about debating who will bear responsibility for this crisis, who will be saddled with the economic cost and who will make the decisions. We cannot speak of climate justice in a system where the polluter takes no responsibility and local people pay for the damage. We cannot leave the responsibility for protecting nature to companies' voluntary commitments and to market mechanisms. At the heart of climate policy there must be an approach in which the peoples defending their living spaces, peasants, working people and scientists have a say. There must be a struggle and a solidarity founded on the value of life. WE NEED AN ORGANISED STRUGGLE THAT CAN PUT FORWARD OUR ALTERNATIVE Nihat Fırat, Kirazlı Ecological Living Association (Kirazlı Ekolojik Yaşam Derneği) Nor is it right to say "They are lying" and simply step aside just because COP31 deceives the people and makes promises. I think we need an organised struggle that can put forward our own alternative forcefully and make each local struggle part of the wider one. We need to be able to set out an alternative, comprehensive programme. Because what we are up against is a huge structure fighting on many fronts. We know that what we are discussing in the context of COP31, the investments capitalists have been trying to make for 31 years to overcome their own structural depressions and crises and to secure their accumulation and their future, is not fair. For a just climate policy to take shape, everyone who, like us, stands on the side of labour must approach this not only in terms of day-to-day interests but, more broadly, on a class basis. No ecological struggle that is not grounded in class is likely to achieve results. Local struggles matter enormously. It is hardly possible to build a general policy without the local. The key thing is for the struggles being waged piecemeal at local level to come together as a whole along an anti-capitalist, anti-imperialist line, and to support rather than hold one another back. That is the whole point. As far as we are concerned, there is no longer any difference between the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and COP31. We are going through a very important period, marked by developments such as the consequences of the climate crisis, the scale the food crisis has reached worldwide and the drought-driven wave of migration that is set to grow even larger. One of the most important dimensions of global warming is the industrial agriculture practised in farming and the industrial livestock farming carried on within it. Especially in our work in rural areas, we need to build serious communication with small family farmers so that people become aware of their own rights. It is the devastation caused by industrial agriculture that is bringing the country, and the world, to this state. Yet at the same time, there are moves to pass brand new laws and take measures to keep industrial agriculture going. Small family producers are being turned into wage slaves on their own land. With this in mind, we need to put the concept of food sovereignty on the agenda of people living in rural areas. There is a declaration adopted by the United Nations (Birleşmiş Milletler) on the rights of peasants and other people living in rural areas. Turkey abstained on it. As people waging struggles on the ground, we must call on political decision makers to bring these demands of ours to the fore as well, and we must take a political stance to that end. I believe we need to set ourselves the task of a serious struggle to have peasants' rights implemented in Turkey too. EVEN IF WE DON'T BELIEVE IN POLITICS, THERE ARE LAWS IN OUR WAY Fatih Onur Demir, Vaminon Good local practice needs to be passed on to other places by sharing experience. The need for a network is something we have also discussed at our meetings. What did we do, what can we do, how did we succeed, how did we fail? These things need to be assessed. If we look at the Artvin example, I know what Neşe abla did there. Going from house to house and coffeehouse to coffeehouse, she reached everyone one to one and tried to explain things to them. This system was explained both through personal relationships and in academic terms. We come from a culture of collective work known in some places as "imece" and here as "meci". Today we all picked kiwis for one of our friends. Tomorrow we will pick them for someone else. Although there may not seem to be as much life in the villages as there once was, in these regions everyone still has one foot in the village. We too need to reach the villages and the village heads (muhtar). Just the other day, this is what we talked about with friends at a meeting: at the next local elections, at least in some strategic areas, we should be the ones who decide which village heads get elected. Because we have come across far too many village heads who, whether through ties to capital, financial hardship or other reasons, turned the whole struggle on its head just to get the village road tarmacked. So we are trying to work on this. But underlying all this, even if we don't believe in politics, there are the laws that politics and the political authorities put in our way. We face threats from mining and hydroelectric power plant (HES) companies that want to come here: "If you don't let us in, we'll come with the security forces." Because a politics that has become the slave of capital, or that is capital itself, cannot find a solution for us. Perhaps this could be solved through an academic framework, through detailed regional study. What can and cannot be done in which region? If there is a need for mining, how much of it, where and in what way can it be done? When Murgul Copper Works (Murgul Bakır İşletmeleri) was first sold to Eti Bakır, a guarantee was given: "We will not use cyanide processing here." But recently, approval was granted for cyanide tanks to be installed. Murgul is just above Arhavi. It is close enough that if someone coughs there, you can hear it here. The water sources there flow down to us, the air comes to us, the soil affects us. Looking at the bigger picture, whether it is COP31 or anything else, we need to change our consumption habits. Nor can we find a solution in a world order where capital is not shared out fairly. That is the case in this country, even in this district. Capital needs to be redistributed and working people need to get what they are owed, so that everyone has financial security and can have a stake in the solution. WE NEED TO UNITE TO ACHIEVE GREAT THINGS Turan Altun, Northern Forests Defence (Kuzey Ormanları Savunması) In the COP31 process, our side is already clear. Capital is carrying out work that destroys the environment and nature. From the government to the opposition, there is nobody who genuinely puts what they say during the COP31 process into practice on the ground. Everyone is doing certain things in words only. Because of the work we did through the Climate Justice Forum (İklim Adaleti Forumu) against COP31, or "Çöp31" ("Rubbish31"), whatever you want to call it, all our Instagram and Twitter accounts were blocked and shut down. I agree with everything my friends and mentors have said. We absolutely must unite. We need to carry all the right, positive work through onto the ground. Where no work is being done, we need to stand together. We must unite so that we can carry out strong work at local level. All these experiences tell us this: the strength of defending living spaces comes from the local, from people's participation, from science, from the law and from volunteer solidarity. Our limits, on the other hand, are set by fear, lack of money, the loss of volunteers and weak institutional solidarity. I still carry on the struggle today in the same spirit. To defend nature is to defend life. This struggle belongs not to any one person, institution or political body; it is a struggle common to us all. Despite everything, we must not lose hope. Volunteering is important and valuable. Because our greatest strength in solving the problems we face today is the volunteers who give their labour in the institutions and civil society organisations we are part of. Once again, it is they who will bring about change and solidarity. Because what we are losing is not just a forest, a stream or a living space; it is our future.
